stem: Arjun invested Rs 50,000 for 2 years. His investment earned a nominal return of 10% in year 1 and 12% in year 2. Inflation was 4% in year 1 and 7% in year 2. Using the Fisher equation applied separately to each year, what is the cumulative real return over the 2-year period (to the nearest 0.01%)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Added the two annual real returns (5.77% + 4.67% = 10.44%) without compounding them multiplicatively, underestimating by ignoring the cross-product of real factors.
Subtracted compound inflation from compound nominal: (1.10 x 1.12 - 1) - (1.04 x 1.07 - 1) = 23.2% - 11.28% = 11.92%, applying simple subtraction to compound factors.
Took simple year-by-year differences (10% - 4%) + (12% - 7%) = 6% + 5% = 11% without applying the Fisher equation or compounding, treating each year as additive.

explanation: Apply Fisher to each year: r_real_yr1 = 1.10/1.04 - 1 = 5.769%; r_real_yr2 = 1.12/1.07 - 1 = 4.673%. Compound the real factors: cumulative = (1.05769)(1.04673) - 1 = 1.10712 - 1 = 10.71%. Never add real returns; compound the (1 + r_real) factors.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two-phase real returns must be compounded as growth factors, not added as percentages.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: apply r_real_yr = (1 + r_nom_yr)/(1 + r_inf_yr) - 1 for each year. Then cumulative = (1 + r1_real)(1 + r2_real) - 1. Year 1: 1.10/1.04 = 1.05769; Year 2: 1.12/1.07 = 1.04673. Product = 1.10712. Cumulative real return = 10.71%.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always compound real growth factors multiplicatively; summing annual real returns ignores the compounding cross-product.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. Two Fisher divisions then one multiplication. The trap options are additive (option 4), non-compounded sum (option 2), and compound nominal minus inflation (option 3).
